title: A picks everything after a clip and moves it as one
goal: A Premiere editor presses A (Track Select Forward) to grab a clip and everything after it, then drags the lot to open or close a gap. Today A on the timeline is still the Arrow tool, because the timeline cannot yet carry more than one clip in a single drag.
notes: Split out of premiere-s-keys-work-on-the-timeline (2026-09-23). The key map already returns .trackSelectForwardTool for A on a focused timeline (Sources/PhotonzCore/TimelineKeys.swift); EditorState+TimelineKeys.perform(timelineCommand:) returns false for it so A falls through to the Arrow tool. Needs: multi-clip carry in ClipPiecesBar.carry / EditorState clipBarDrag (one layer today), and a third tool beside Select and Blade in TimelineDock.localBar (isTimelineBlade becomes a tool enum). The mock (docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html) draws only Select and Blade, so a third button goes beyond it; keep it the same size and face.
acceptance: With the timeline holding the keyboard, A picks up a Track Select Forward tool in the timeline bar, and V puts it down
A click on a clip with that tool picks it and every clip that starts at or after it, on every track (Shift-A: that track only)
Dragging any picked clip moves every picked clip by the same amount, in one undo step
A walk with no flags set presses A, clicks a clip, drags, and claims where each clip landed
Works at Next defaults with no switch turned on, and an audit written under queue/audits/ gives the try steps and a real picture
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
